section_entries.label: 5. Symmetric base point, shadow zeta, and continuation
section_entries.mathematical_role: Moves to the symmetric zero shift, models trivial zeros and the zeta pole as a shadow spectrum, derives explicit Mellin/Hankel continuation formulas, extracts poles and trace identities, and sketches extension to other zeta/L-functions.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: At the symmetric shift, resolvent terms split into explicit shadow and residual Mellin pieces
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Uses factorization, a regularized trivial-zero resolvent, contour rotation, Hankel conversion, and residue calculus to separate an explicit shadow-zeta term from a residual integral and obtain conjugate and principal-value continuations.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: The explicit shadow term controls poles, trace identities, and a resummed prime asymptotic
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Shows that the residual integral is regular in the target half-plane, so pole and integer-value data come from the shadow term, and relates the large-negative-parameter expansion to a resummation of Guinand’s divergent prime series.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The new Mellin representations serve as secondary-zeta analogues of the original functional equation: they are useful not merely because they continue the function, but because they expose the ingredients controlling that continuation.
